findings.highlight: One only dies when their will is gone.
findings.evidenceJa: 意思がなくなれば死ぬだけ
findings.governingReading: Once his remaining will disappears, nothing remains for him but death.
findings.explanation: “Only” changes the relation between will and death. The Japanese says that without his will, only death remains; the English says death occurs only when the will is gone. The following page preserves the original reasoning.

findings.governingReading: 痛烈に憧れた names a piercing/intense longing for what he could not do himself.
findings.explanation: Painfully intense admiration becomes admiring severely.
